title: VPC segmentation & egress patterns onboarding notes
content:
Purpose:
This working note captures recommended segmentation topologies and egress strategies we should use when onboarding new customer VPCs (cloud-hosted or air-gapped on-prem edge equivalents). It synthesizes recent onboarding learnings and includes Terraform module notes and an upgrade/migration checklist that ops and solutions-engineering can use as a baseline.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: solutions-engineering, platform SREs, private-deployments delivery engineers, and customers' network teams.
- Scope: network segmentation (control/data/admin), cross-VPC routing options, egress/proxy patterns, Terraform primitives and upgrade concerns for existing customer VPCs. Does NOT cover cloud account provisioning, KMS/HSM key exchange details, or host-level security hardening (those live in separate docs).

Context and guiding constraints (assumptions):
- Customers want minimal surface area for telemetry while preserving control-plane connectivity for rollouts.
- Many customers restrict direct egress: egress often must be routed through approved proxies or enforced with firewall policies.
- We must support two primary deployment models: (1) VPC in customer cloud with peering/transit gateway, (2) Private deployment in customer on-prem with software routers/SD-WAN.
- Terraform modules are the preferred delivery mechanism for reproducible, reviewable infra across both models.

Recommended segmentation (high level):
- mgmt-subnet(s): control plane endpoints (Redwood agent, health checks, metrics push). High-availability across AZs, small CIDR allocation (e.g., /26 per AZ).
- compute-subnets: GPU/serving nodes. Large CIDR (dependent on cluster size). Optionally split into accelerated-subnet and cpu-subnet for licensing/size differences.
- provisioning-subnet: ephemeral provisioning/packer/ops tasks. Restricted inbound rules.
- tooling-subnet: egress-enabled sidecars/proxies, NAT gateways and restricted egress.
- storage-subnet: object-store endpoints & internal storage services if colocated. Keep tightly restricted to serving and mgmt.

Segmentation patterns (concrete patterns to propose):
- Pattern A (Transit-first): Transit Gateway / Shared VPC central egress. Pros: central visibility, per-customer policy. Cons: added complexity, infra cost. Recommended for enterprises.
- Pattern B (Edge-proxy): Per-VPC egress via a managed proxy (squid/nginx) in tooling-subnet with strict egress allowlist. Pros: minimal cross-account plumbing, easier audit. Cons: single point for outbound; need HA.
- Pattern C (Air-gapped/on-prem): Local appliance + queued telemetry. Control plane uses customer-approved bastion/agent for rollouts; telemetry batched to an internal collector; optional offline bundle flow for model updates.

Egress & outbound recommendations:
- Do not require direct internet access from compute-subnet. Prefer proxied egress through tooling-subnet or customer's NGFW.
- Allowlist TLS endpoints for package repositories, container registries, image signing services, and Redwood control-plane (list kept in confluence). Use FQDN-based allowlists where possible to reduce CIDR churn.
- For model downloads: use signed manifests + pre-approved object-store endpoints reachable via VPC endpoints (private link) to avoid public egress.
- Telemetry: prefer pushing metrics through a local collector inside tooling-subnet that forwards outbound on a single port to customer-approved destinations.

Terraform module notes (developer-oriented):
- Module layout recommendation (flat, composable):
  - modules/vpc-core: creates VPC, subnets, route tables, core SGs. Inputs: vpc_cidr, azs, subnet_sizes_map. Outputs: subnet_ids_map, route_table_ids.
  - modules/egress-proxy: provisioning of proxy ASG/instance profile, autoscaling, and health checks. Inputs: proxy_image, instance_type, allowed_egress_destinations (list of FQDNs/CIDRs). Outputs: proxy_dns, proxy_elb.
  - modules/transit-attachements: transit gateway or peering attachments. Inputs: owner_account, route_propagation_map. Outputs: attachment_id, propagations.
  - examples/customer-onboarding: opinionated composition of the above with variables surfaced for customer-facing review.
- Versioning: tag modules semver; each onboarding uses a commit/tag. Make small upgrades opt-in.
- State handling: prefer remote state per-customer (separate backend bucket with encryption). Avoid shared remote state between different customers.
- Idempotency/immutability: modules should avoid in-place replacement for route tables and NATs unless explicitly requested. Provide migration plan outputs when changing resources that cause replacements.

Inputs we ask customer for (minimal list):
- primary_vpc_cidr and reserved CIDRs for host/pods
- list of allowed egress FQDNs / CIDRs and any blocking proxies
- required AZs and desired capacity per AZ (GPU count)
- KMS key ARN + IAM principals for Terraform state/encryption
- contact: network owner + SOC contact + jump-host details

Onboarding checklist (pre-deploy, deploy, validation):
- Pre-deploy (Done before Terraform apply):
  - Confirm CIDR plan and AZ quotas.
  - Collect allowlist endpoints and KMS ARNs.
  - Confirm telemetry destinations and port allowances.
  - Create remote state bucket and grant service account access for CI.
  - Open a security review ticket if customer requires additional controls.
- Deploy:
  - Run terraform plan in isolated account with explain output.
  - Apply in canary AZ (or smallest capacity) with monitoring enabled.
  - Verify route tables, SGs, and proper subnet isolation.
- Validation:
  - Health-check: control-plane agent registers in our console.
  - Egress smoke tests: package fetch test, image pull test, telemetry push test.
  - Load test: synthetic single-instance throughput to ensure kernel optimizations are available.
  - Observability: logs flow to expected sinks and cost/latency metrics appear in console.

Upgrade & migration considerations (for customers with existing VPCs):
- Non-disruptive attachment approach: create new tooling-subnet + proxy stack then migrate routes incrementally. Do not replace default route table without a rollback path.
- When adding Transit Gateway attachments: create propagation routes in stages and monitor BGP or route-leakage depending on cloud.
- NAT -> Proxy migration: instantiate proxy in private subnet; update route table association for a small portion of subnets, validate, then flip remainers.
- Terraform: use import to bring existing resources into module-managed state before making changes. Document each import in the PR.

Common pitfalls & mitigations:
- Pitfall: customer has overlapping CIDRs. Mitigation: recommend NAT + proxy pattern or suggest renumbering; provide small RFC template to help customer.
- Pitfall: overly-broad security groups used by customer. Mitigation: run a scan, provide stepwise tightening plan and a test harness.
- Pitfall: image registry egress blocked by corporate proxy. Mitigation: validate registry access early, use mirrored registry inside the customer network where possible.

Quick runbook (minimal steps to onboard a new customer):
1) Intake call: capture CIDRs, AZs, allowlist, contacts.
2) Create TF workspace + remote state.
3) Template TF variables file for customer and run plan.
4) Apply to canary AZ.
5) Run smoke tests; collect logs and screenshots.
6) Ramp to full capacity and enable rollout policies.
7) Hand-off: create runbook page in customer Confluence with ops playbook and escalation path.

Rollback & incident notes:
- Always keep a pre-deploy snapshot of route table associations and SG rules.
- If control-plane agent fails to register after deploy, revert route changes and route agent traffic to earlier proxy.
- For critical egress failures, switch to customer-provided emergency bastion (pre-agreed) to run diagnostic commands.

Open questions / items to follow-up:
- Should we publish a small sentinel agent image that verifies egress endpoints (TLS + FQDN) instead of relying on ephemeral tests?
- When can we standardize on a single proxy module across all customers vs allowing runbook-level custom proxies?
- Need to create a small DFIR checklist for handling suspected telemetry exfil.

Notes for next iteration:
- Add diagrams (transit vs proxy) that map directly to module outputs.
- Produce a Terraform migration helper script that generates import commands for common cloud provider resources.

Appendix: quick snippets / useful commands:
- terraform import aws_route_table.rtable rtb-123456 -> note and capture in PR.
- curl --resolve proxy.example:443:10.0.5.10 https://proxy.example/health -> used for proxy health-check from canary instance.

End of notes.

(Informal: this doc is deliberately pragmatic — capture early wins and we can extract a formal playbook after 3–4 onboardings.)
